entries.title: Psalms 109:1
segments:
PSALM CIX. 
 
  David complains of his enemies and appeals to God, ver. 1-5.   Foretells their destruction, ver. 6-20.   Prays that God would succour him in his low condition, ver. 21-29.   Concludes with a joyful hope of deliverance, ver. 30, 31   To the chief musician, A psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. God-The author and matter of all my praises.

entries.title: Psalms 109:4
segments: V. 4. Adversaries-They requite my love with enmity, as it is explained ver.

entries.title: Psalms 109:6
segments: V. 6. A wicked man-Who will rule him with rigour and cruelty. Satan-To accuse him; for this was the place and posture of accusers in the Jewish courts.

entries.title: Psalms 109:7
segments: V. 7. Sin-Because it is not from his heart.

entries.title: Psalms 109:10
segments: V. 10. Desolate places-Into which they are fled for fear and shame.

entries.title: Psalms 109:11
segments: V. 11. Catch-Heb. ensnare, take away not only by oppression but also by cunning artificers.  Stranger-Who hath no right to his goods.

entries.title: Psalms 109:17
segments: V. 17. Delighted not-In desiring and promoting the welfare of others.

entries.title: Psalms 109:18
segments: V. 18. Garment-Which a man wears constantly.  Like water-Water in the cavity of the belly, between the bowels, is almost certain death. And oil soaking into any of the bones, will soon utterly destroy it.

entries.title: Psalms 109:20
segments: V. 20. That speak evil against my soul-With design to take away my life.

entries.title: Psalms 109:21
segments: V. 21. Is good-Above the mercy of all the creatures.

entries.title: Psalms 109:23
segments: V. 23. When-Towards the evening, when the sun is setting. The locust-Which is easily driven away with every wind.
